## Current consolidated truth
The Larkspur ferry inspection is on @VALUE@ (@ID@). It was first set for May 14 and then moved; the earlier date is history, kept as claim C4 and superseded by C1. Wenna Ostrow leads the inspection crew, and the crew budget is 3,200 crowns. The crew keeps paper logbooks on the ferry because the deck tablets fog up in the spray, which is a practical lesson about equipment on open water rather than a preference. Nothing in the thread suggests the budget changed when the date moved, so the budget claim stands as filed.

The thread is short and settled: one decision (the date), one person in charge (Wenna Ostrow), one amount (the budget), and one working habit (paper logbooks). The date is the only value that changed. Anyone planning around the inspection should use the live date above and not the first one. The inspection crew will need the ferry out of service for the day of the inspection, and the schedule of the crossing will need a notice to passengers a week ahead, which the thread names as an open item rather than a decision. The thread does not say who writes that notice, so it stays open below.

The working habit deserves a sentence of its own, because it is the kind of thing that is lost first in a summary: the paper logbooks are not nostalgia, they are a response to a specific failure of the deck tablets in wet conditions. If the tablets are ever replaced by a model that tolerates spray, the reason for the paper logbooks goes away, and the habit can be revisited then; until then the logbooks stay.
